{"name":"split-scenes","procedure":"If the session has no stored transcript, upload the transcript yourself. With a shell and a file on disk, call transcript_upload_url and run curl -T <file> <signed-url> directly from disk. Never read, echo, cat or repeat the file to upload it. The signed URL is single-use and expires after ten minutes.
Without a shell, send the transcript you hold in context through transcript_append {session, chunk, index, final}. Send exact consecutive chunks of at most 64000 UTF-8 bytes, starting at index 0 and increasing by 1, with at most 128 chunks. Use larger chunks for a long transcript; restart with larger chunks if you reach that count. Do not summarize, omit or alter text, timestamps, speakers, whitespace or line endings; do not split a Unicode character. Set final: true only on the last chunk. Only uploaded: true confirms the complete transcript is stored. A response with uploaded: false accepts a chunk, not the transcript. Retry an identical chunk with the same index and final after a lost reply; use nextIndex to recover an out-of-order request. If the content must change, an incomplete upload must be cancelled, or the one-hour chunk upload expires, send restart: true with index 0, then resend all chunks. Each tool call goes through the model, so this path costs output tokens; with a shell always use the signed URL instead.
Both paths use UTF-8 [HH:MM:SS] Speaker: text with continuation lines, at most 8 MB and 20000 utterances, 32 KB per utterance including continuations. Upload before scenes or draft changes exist. Never echo the transcript in chat. Never ask the game master to upload when a tool path exists. The pageUrl from transcript_upload_url is a fallback only if the client cannot access the transcript through either path. Read get transcript:<session> to confirm it is stored.
Load skill map-speakers and map the speakers. Read get transcript:<session> in pages or timestamp windows; follow nextCursor as cursor with the same ref while truncated. Never repeat the transcript in output.
Split into scenes at changes of place or situation. Give each a short title, start and optional end timestamp, place and a summary of plot points in one or two lines. Keep the original timestamps. Do not overlap scenes. Leave out rolls, rests, hit points and inventory.
Call scenes_set with the session and scenes in order. Use get scene:<session>/<n> to check a scene with its utterances. Splitting replaces earlier scenes, so drop existing draft changes first; a committed debrief and its scenes are closed.

Standing rules
Never draft prep. Propose only on the game master's explicit request, at most three situations built from story-state facts with sources.
Ask about situations and pressure, never player decisions or outcomes.
Story state records what happened. The adventure frame records intent. Keep them apart.
Write in the game master's language.","skills":[]}

scenes.title: Dusk at the Glass Causeway
scenes.summary: The party arrives at dusk with the river gate closing in four bells. Sera Venn urges them toward her ferry, mentions the Lantern Widow under the bridge, and shows a broken seal; the gate clock has four segments, one filled. Rowan suspects Sera works for the raiders and wants to ask the gatekeeper about the seal.

scenes.title: Red Cord at the Ferry Landing
scenes.summary: At the ferry landing the gatekeeper leaves a red cord tied to the post while the party is still there at dusk.
